title: California janitorial employer registration covers defined contractor and franchise arrangements
activity: Employing or arranging work in the state
affectedParty: Operating entity and responsible payroll or compliance manager
applicability: Persons or entities within the janitorial employer definition, including covered contractual, subcontractual and franchise arrangements.
requirement: A defined janitorial employer must register with the Labor Commissioner even where covered workers perform predominantly janitorial work as contractors or franchisees. Current program guidance states a $500 initial fee, annual $500 renewal and three-year records; determine the actual provider and recipient roles before applying the FAQ exclusions.
exceptions: The agency FAQ excludes residential-only cleaning providers and service recipients acting as recipients, and interprets the program as applying to private entities. Covered-worker and actual-role facts remain necessary.
trigger: Providing covered janitorial services or arranging their provision as a defined employer
deadline: Register for covered operations; renewal due annually by the original issuance month and day
renewal: Annual; agency states a $500 renewal fee.
interpretationLimits: Narrow stated issue; not comprehensive state, federal, sector or local clearance.

title: California janitorial training has frequency, provider and evidence requirements
activity: Employing or arranging work in the state
affectedParty: Operating entity and responsible payroll or compliance manager
applicability: Covered janitorial employers and their nonsupervisory covered workers and supervisors; covered workers can include contractors and franchisees.
requirement: For covered janitorial employers, ensure at least two hours of sexual-violence and harassment prevention training at least every two years for nonsupervisory covered workers and their supervisors, and within six months of a new position. Use the required content and qualified-provider route; retain required evidence for at least three years. The employer bears the proof burden even when another entity provides training.
exceptions: Section 13821(a)(1) permits a defined covered successor employer to use a retained worker’s documented last-training date only if its workforce-retention, seniority, wage and policy conditions are satisfied.
trigger: Before committing to the covered work or payroll arrangement
deadline: At least every two years; within six months of assuming a new covered position
renewal: Training cycle is separate from annual janitorial registration renewal.
evidence: Content, signed DLSE 800 form and required payment certification
Records retained at least three years
interpretationLimits: Narrow stated issue; not comprehensive state, federal, sector or local clearance.

title: California 2026 general minimum wage is a floor requiring location and industry checks
activity: Employing or arranging work in the state

exceptions: MW-2026 contains applicability exceptions and identifies separate fast-food and healthcare requirements. Local rates may exceed the general state floor.

title: California executive exemption requires actual duties as well as salary
activity: Employing or arranging work in the state
affectedParty: Operating entity and responsible payroll or compliance manager
applicability: Apply the named rule to the actual work, entity, worker and location facts.
requirement: DLSE describes cumulative executive-exemption conditions: management of the enterprise or a recognized unit, regular direction of two or more employees, hiring/firing authority or weighted recommendations, discretion and independent judgment, primarily exempt duties, and a salary of at least twice the state minimum wage for full-time employment. A manager title or total employment budget does not establish this exemption.
exceptions: Other exemptions and the correct wage order require separate analysis; this record does not decide the administrative, professional, outside-sales or computer exemptions.
trigger: Before committing to the covered work or payroll arrangement
deadline: Before the covered arrangement; ongoing compliance as applicable
evidence: Guaranteed salary terms distinguished from benefits and employer costs

title: Texas TWC unemployment-tax classification turns on actual direction and control
activity: Employing or arranging work in the state
affectedParty: Operating entity and responsible payroll or compliance manager
applicability: Texas Unemployment Compensation Act worker classification as explained by the Texas Workforce Commission.
requirement: For Texas unemployment-tax purposes, TWC identifies service, wages and direction/control and applies a 20-factor common-law guide. The right to control can suffice without actual exercise. Factor relevance and weight vary with the facts; a 1099 or contractor agreement does not determine status.
exceptions: This is not a determination under federal wage law, federal tax law, another state’s law, or a transaction-specific ruling.
trigger: Before committing to the covered work or payroll arrangement
deadline: Before the covered arrangement; ongoing compliance as applicable
evidence: Actual control and performance facts for each relevant factor
Scheduling, training, tools, payment and substitution evidence
Reasoned assessment or TWC inquiry rather than a numeric factor score

title: New York 2026 payroll planning requires the actual region and wage order
activity: Employing or arranging work in the state
affectedParty: Operating entity and responsible payroll or compliance manager
applicability: Apply the named rule to the actual work, entity, worker and location facts.
requirement: Dated NYDOL 2026 miscellaneous and building-service posters state $17 per hour for New York City, Long Island and Westchester County and $16 elsewhere in New York State. Determine the correct industry and worker category; the building-service poster has distinct residential janitor provisions and extra-pay/credit rules. Rates alone do not settle overtime, uniform maintenance, call-in pay or exemption eligibility.
exceptions: Industry-specific rates, residential janitor arrangements, allowed credits and exemptions require their own conditions. No hospitality tip credit is imported into miscellaneous or building-service work.
trigger: Before committing to the covered work or payroll arrangement
deadline: Cited 2026 posters apply January 1 through December 31, 2026; recheck for the actual payroll period
evidence: Correct wage order and worker category
Hours, extra-pay, uniform and credit review
